LOX/methane impinging injector

LOX/methane impinging injector

60 unlike doublets in four rings take the main fuel and all the oxidizer. An outer ring of 30 single fuel jets, leaning 15° outward, strikes the wall 26 mm downstream of the face and spreads along it as a film. The film ring is fed from its own source at 1.30·p_c, higher than the main fuel plenum's 1.15·p_c. The scene shows the wetted surface: each hole's bore, coloured by feed, ending at the face plate. The grey arrows are not hardware; each points from a hole to the impingement point it is aimed at. Colour the scene by Hole mass flow or Jet velocity to see the drilled injector at the design plenum pressures. The grey disc is the chamber, 130 mm across.

The drilled injector, seen into the chamber (+x)
Hover a hole for its set, element and diameter.

Design point and choices

The injector is designed to deliver 6 kg/s of oxygen at 95 K and 1.9 kg/s of methane at 120 K into a 60 bar face, 10 % of the fuel through the film ring: an overall mixture ratio of 3.16. Every choice below is supplied, not solved for. Each hole is sized for its share of its feed's flow at its feed's pressure drop, with Orifice.sized, and then rounded to the nearest 0.05 mm drill.

Feed Fluid Plenum / p_c Cd L [mm] Holes Designed d [mm] Drilled d [mm] Inclination [°]
Main fuel plenum Methane 1.15 0.75 6 60 1.33 1.35 30.0
Oxidizer plenum Oxygen 1.20 0.75 7 60 1.805 1.8 11.7
Film ring Methane 1.30 0.72 4 30 0.5379 0.55 15.0

The fuel jet of each unlike doublet leans 30° towards the element axis. The oxidizer jet carries more momentum, so it leans only 11.7°: then the two jets' sideways momenta cancel and the spray leaves along the axis. Equal angles would have tipped it off the axis towards the fuel hole's side.

Rupe found mixing most uniform with his ratio near one. At 1.78 the oxidizer jets overpower the fuel jets. Since ρv²d grows as about Δp^0.75 at a fixed flow, raising the fuel pressure drop or lowering the oxidizer one closes the gap. The stiffness split here is kept for its margin on each side, and the ratio is left as a report.

Layout checks

The film jets are aimed at the wall on purpose, so their impingement points sit on it and leave no clearance. The holes themselves stay clear of it.

What rounding the holes to drills did

Two questions, one injector. At design pressures: each plenum is held at its design pressure and the flows are whatever the drilled holes pass. At design flows: each feed passes its design flow and the plenum pressure is whatever it takes. The design column is what the holes were sized for.

Setting the film share with the ring pressure

The film ring and the main fuel plenum are separate feeds, so the film holes' flow depends on the film ring's own pressure and nothing else. Holding the main plenums at their design pressures and moving the film ring shows how the film share responds. Across this range it runs from 6.1 % to 12.7 % of the fuel. How the ring pressure is set, and what it costs the pump, is the feed system's question, not the injector's. The marked point is the drilled injector at the design ring pressure: 10.13 % against the 10 % the holes were sized for, since rounding to drills changed both the film and the main fuel holes.
